title: Service outage — customer brief and status-post draft
body:
PURPOSE:
This is a customer-facing draft that combines a concise status-page update for immediate posting and a short post-incident summary for customers who want the facts and remediation plan. Intended audience: affected customers and account teams. Tone: clear, non-technical where possible, accountable.

STATUS PAGE UPDATE (to be posted immediately) — SHORT FORM:
Title: Service degradation affecting hosted inference (June 18, 2026)
Impact: From ~08:17–09:03 UTC on 2026-06-18, a subset of requests to the Redwood hosted API experienced elevated error rates and increased latency. Some customers saw failed requests and delayed responses.
Current status: Resolved (09:03 UTC). Full mitigation completed; routing and capacity fallbacks are stable.
What we’re doing: We performed traffic rerouting and a targeted configuration rollback to restore normal request handling. We are continuing verification and additional hardening steps; customers may see transient retries for a short window.
ETA for next update: 2026-06-19 15:00 UTC or sooner if new information is available.

CUSTOMER-FACING POSTMORTEM SUMMARY (concise)
Summary: On 2026-06-18 at 08:17 UTC, Redwood observed a service degradation affecting the hosted inference API that resulted in higher-than-normal request failures and latencies for a subset of customers. We reverted a recent routing/configuration change and routed traffic to alternate capacity pools; normal service resumed by 09:03 UTC.
Scope of impact: Intermittent request errors (5xx) and higher latencies for approximately 18% of traffic for the hosted API region us-west-2 during the window. No customer data was exposed. Dedicated and Private deployments were not affected.
Root cause (summary): A configuration change to the smart-routing policy (deploy id: rbt-route-4f2) combined with a concurrent autoscaler edge-case resulted in a feedback loop: sudden rebalancing attempts caused repeated connection churn, which led to queue buildup on a routing tier and subsequent request failures.
Immediate mitigation: Within 14 minutes of detection we rolled back the routing change and applied a temporary cap on rebalancing actions. Traffic was re-routed to stable pools and connection pools were drained gracefully. Error rates returned to baseline by 09:03 UTC.
Customer impact detail:
- Affected customers: Customers using Redwood hosted API endpoints in region us-west-2 who had traffic routed through the rebalanced pools.
- Typical symptoms: 502/503 responses, increased per-request latency, and occasional streaming interruptions.
- Duration: Peak impact from 08:19–08:55 UTC; full recovery observed at 09:03 UTC.

What we’ve done since:
1) Reverted the routing policy change and restored prior routing configuration.
2) Implemented an emergency throttle on rebalancing events to prevent the autoscaler feedback loop.
3) Cleared and rebuilt affected connection pools; verified health checks and warm caches on fallback pools.
4) Notified on-call SRE and serving-runtime engineering teams for follow-up investigation.

Planned next steps (short-term):
- Root-cause deep dive (in progress): running additional telemetry correlation to identify the precise interaction vector between the routing change and autoscaler thresholds. Target: complete by 2026-06-22.
- Post-incident configuration guardrails: add validation and staged rollout checks for routing changes to prevent fast rebalancing on high-traffic prefixes.
- Improved alerting: refine signal thresholds so we detect similar queue-growth patterns earlier and surface mitigations automatically.
- Customer outreach: account teams will send personalized notes to customers who experienced >=10% error rate for longer than 10 minutes.

Compensation and credits
We recognize the operational impact this outage caused. Customers directly impacted will be eligible for a one-time service credit proportional to incident exposure, as outlined in the SLA. Account teams will follow up with a proposed credit amount.

Recommended customer actions
- If you saw transient failures: implement client-side retry/backoff if you have short-lived synchronous requests.
- For streaming workloads: validate resumed sessions and reconnect clients if necessary.
- If you still observe errors or degraded performance in us-west-2: open a support ticket with request traces and timestamps; include request ids where available.

Frequently asked questions (short)
Q: Was customer data exposed? A: No. This incident was an availability issue; there is no evidence of data exfiltration.
Q: Were Dedicated or Private deployments affected? A: No. Only hosted API traffic routed through the affected pools in us-west-2 was impacted.
Q: Will this happen again? A: We have immediate mitigations in place and longer-term guardrails planned; our post-incident engineering backlog includes configuration validation and autoscaler safeguards to reduce recurrence risk.

Contacts and escalation
- Primary contact: Customer Success, customer-success@redwood.ai (for account-level follow-up)
- Urgent operational issues / technical traces: support@redwood.ai and file INC-2026 with the Jira link provided.

DRAFT NOTES FOR INTERNAL USE (short)
- Keep the status page short and factual; minimize technical detail there.
- This draft should be reviewed by eng-serving-runtime and SRE for accuracy on the timeline and root cause phrasing before publishing the postmortem section.
- Suggested PS: include a short technical appendix for customer engineers who request more detail (to be attached as a separate doc).

APPENDIX: Concise timeline (timestamps UTC)
- 08:12 Detectable increase in queue length on routing tier (automated metric alert threshold X1 triggered)
- 08:17 Error rate climbs above baseline; CS monitors receive initial reports from customers
- 08:22 Routing config change (rbt-route-4f2) deployed (intended to improve distribution)
- 08:26 Autoscaler reacts to transient load and triggers rebalancing wave; connection churn increases
- 08:34 Error rates spike; SRE paged; mitigation planning begins
- 08:39 Decision to rollback routing change; emergency throttle policy prepared
- 08:47 Routing rollback executed; traffic begins migrating away from unstable pools
- 08:55 Error rate trending down; connection pool drains in progress
- 09:03 Error rates back to baseline; incident declared resolved (monitoring remains active)

FOR ACCOUNT TEAMS
- Suggested subject line for outreach: "Update: Redwood hosted API service interruption — summary and next steps"
- Suggested one-paragraph template: "Hi <Customer>, we saw an outage affecting hosted API requests in us-west-2 on Jun 18 between 08:17–09:03 UTC. We reverted a routing configuration change and applied safeguards; no customer data was affected. Your account team will reach out if you were directly impacted. We apologize for the disruption and are implementing follow-up prevention steps. — Jordan Patel, Customer Success"

END OF DRAFT
